characterList.name: Narrator (Calvin)

content_metadata.description: A guided tour of the Stellarium software, showcasing its features as a home planetarium tool to make space exploration accessible.

qAndA.answer: Around 5.82 degrees (visible in the bottom bar of the software interface at 2:20).
qAndA.question: What is the approximate field of view when the narrator zooms in on Jupiter?

qAndA.answer: To demonstrate that Stellarium can reveal stars even during daylight, highlighting its ability to bypass real-world limitations.
qAndA.question: Why does the narrator turn off the atmosphere even when the sun is up?
What are the two types of telescope mounts mentioned in the video?

qAndA.answer: The date and time in the bottom right corner of the interface start to decrease, showcasing the reverse time travel functionality.
qAndA.question: How can you tell the time is going backwards in Stellarium?

qAndA.answer: Making space exploration and stargazing accessible to everyone through the free and user-friendly Stellarium software.

Shift from curious to content as night mode is enabled, making the view more comfortable and user-friendly.

narrativeProgression.description: Demonstration and explanation of Stellarium functionalities.
Shift focus from basic navigation to enabling/disabling various display options.
Introduction of the centering and locking feature, allowing users to track specific objects.
Highlighting the time travel functionality, a key aspect of Stellarium's appeal.
Introduction of grids and constellation options, demonstrating the customization capabilities.
Demonstrating the location change feature, emphasizing the global accessibility of the software.
Using the search function to locate specific celestial objects.
Briefly showing the configuration window for further customization.

youtube_description:
This is a quick introduction to Stellarium, the free planetarium software. It will be interesting to those who have not heard of it before and want to see it in action. Get Stellarium for free at their website: https://stellarium.org/


This video is part of our ExoExploration video series. ExoExplorations is a set of lessons, activity and information on astronomy topics at the grade school level. Check it out at https://centreoftheuniverse.org/exoexplorations



Friends of the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory is a charitable organization based in Victoria, BC dedicated to promoting public science outreach at the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory.
We are revitalizing its public programming and visitors centre, the "centre of the universe".

Website: centreoftheuniverse.org
Facebook Page: facebook.com/FriendsDAO
